items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’ve played John Coltrane tunes... you can’t forget that a big part of improvising is forgetting what you know... this is what John Coltrane did when he played this.

ctx.x: Yeah. It really strikes me how fast jazz has moved along in its history and sometimes I wonder if it almost isn’t too fast.

Yeah, well maybe in a way. But the amazing thing, with all those changes is that people still — musicians and listeners can be very closed minded and say I just like music of the 1930s, I just like to listen to Coltrane and beyond. There’s so much out there that you could listen to and love and why limit yourself to one small little gap of time? So I really try to play and listen to as many things as I can. And even if I’m playing an old standard, somehow all these things are filtered into my playing. For me, if…
Yeah, in my opinion when a Crusaders tune was done, you could hum the tune back.
